summary.text: A deep-sea community is any group of organisms sharing a habitat in the deep sea, a remote biome that is still largely unexplored.
Because of high pressure, extreme temperatures and no light, scientists long believed little lived there, but research since the 19th century has found significant biodiversity.
Below the sunlit layer the sea is permanently dark, so deep-sea life runs on marine snow, whale falls, and chemosynthesis at hydrothermal vents and cold seeps.

facts.label: Main energy sources
facts.value: Marine snow, whale falls, vent and seep chemosynthesis

facts.label: Pressure increase
facts.value: About one atmosphere every ten meters

facts.label: Early discoveries
facts.value: Challenger expedition, 1870s, found many varied creatures

items.prompt: A submersible sinks 100 meters deeper into the sea. Roughly how much does the water pressure on its hull go up?

options.label: About 1 atmosphere
About 10 atmospheres
About 100 atmospheres
About 1,000 atmospheres

items.explain: Pressure rises by about one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth, so 100 meters adds about ten.

items.prompt: A fish lives 3 km down in total darkness, far from any vent or seep. Where does its food ultimately come from?

options.label: Algae growing on the rocks beside it
Heat rising out of the seafloor
Minerals soaked up through its skin
Material sinking from the water above

items.explain: Without light there is no photosynthesis, so life in the dark zone must swim up to feed, rely on material sinking from above, or use chemical energy at vents and seeps.

items.prompt: Before the 1800s, why did scientists expect the deep ocean to hold very little life?

options.label: Its pressure, temperatures and darkness seemed too hostile
Deep water was thought to contain no salt at all
Fishermen's nets had only ever brought up mud
Deep water was believed to be too acidic

items.explain: High pressure, extreme temperatures and the absence of light made the deep sea look like a hostile place, so life there was assumed to be sparse.

items.prompt: Geologists exploring the seafloor stumbled on the first deep-sea animal community that runs on chemical energy instead of sunlight. Where were they?

options.label: Under thick Arctic sea ice
Around a sunken whale skeleton
At hydrothermal vents in the Pacific
On a shallow coral reef

items.explain: The first chemosynthetic community with higher animals was found, unexpectedly, at hydrothermal vents in the eastern Pacific during geological work.

items.prompt: Compare a fish caught at 500 m with a related fish living far deeper. What would you expect of the deeper one's body?

options.label: Heavier bones to resist the pressure
Thicker scales and a tougher skin
Jellier flesh and a lighter skeleton
A much larger, bulkier body overall

items.explain: The deeper these animals live, the more gelatinous their flesh and the more minimal their skeleton; many deep fish are also small.

items.prompt: A dead whale settles onto the dark seafloor. What does it mean for the deep-sea community there?

options.label: A major source of energy and nutrients
A poison that drives the local animals away
Shelter only, since deep animals cannot eat it
Nothing, because it floats back to the surface

items.explain: Whale falls are one of the three main sources of energy and nutrients for deep-sea communities, alongside marine snow and chemosynthesis.
